target_customer: Mobile app developers and publishers that want in-app purchase of products from third-party retailers
problem: Mobile checkout across many retailers was slow and fragmented, so apps and publishers could not let shoppers buy inside the app.
business_model: Usage-based API for publishers and apps, with retailer integrations and order guarantee

founders.name: Razvan Roman
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a repeat founder; led fundraising, sales and the company sale.

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating checkout across hundreds of retailer sites with an order guarantee needed scraping and integration engineering that is ongoing work, though standard web technology.

defensibility.rationale: Retailer integrations took effort but were copyable, and checkout depended on third-party retailer sites that could change.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in sourced material; Honey Science acquired it in November 2019, later itself acquired by PayPal.

market_need_then: By August 2014 Two Tap reported working with 215 retailers and apps including Kiip, Shopsy and Wanelo, which was testing an in-app buy button (Retail Dive, August 2014).

branding.domain_note: twotap.com, exact match .com listed on YC page.
branding.brand_signature: Two taps to buy, implied by the name

brand_strength.rationale: The name described the product promise but searches found no press on the brand itself, no mascot or community.

outcome_analysis: Two Tap raised a $2.7 million seed in August 2014 from Khosla and others and grew a retailer and app network, but no later rounds were found. It was sold to Honey Science in November 2019 on terms not public, which the sources do not describe as a large outcome. Why it stalled is not public.
notes: twotap.com did not resolve in this session (network block), not necessarily dead. Seed confirmed by TechCrunch headline and Retail Dive; one aggregator gives $3M. Exit date 2019-11 comes from a deal aggregator (mergerlinks) and the acquirer from the YC page; Crunchbase and CB Insights snippets say closed, a conflict. No dated competitors found in the sources opened. Later added automated inventory and international shopping; dates not verified, so no pivot recorded.
